extracted.intended_audience: Singapore public, businesses, NGOs and policymakers interested in Singapore's decarbonisation policy and public consultation outcomes
extracted.subtask_description: Summary of public responses to the REACH online consultation on Singapore's decarbonisation journey (8 Oct–5 Nov 2024), reporting quantitative support levels and summarising qualitative suggestions and concerns about targets, measures, incentives and consultation design.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support for net zero by 2050
rubrics_metrics.description: Level of public support for Singapore's goal to achieve net zero emissions by 2050.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported finding: 91% of respondents were supportive. Reasons for support included 'we should do more so that our future generations can have a more liveable environment' and 'we should do more to reduce the worst effects of climate change on ourselves'. For those unsupportive, main reasons were cost to individuals and effects on economic competitiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ambition and acceleration of targets
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether Singapore should further accelerate its transition to net zero and set more ambitious climate targets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Of those supportive of net zero, 82% stated Singapore should further accelerate and set more ambitious targets. Suggested practices include setting interim goals towards net zero and reporting progress of decarbonisation measures to increase transparency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance with cost of living and competitiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: Consideration of economic competitiveness and household costs when designing decarbonisation policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some respondents urged fewer resources on climate action to prioritise lowering cost of living and business costs. Policies (e.g., carbon tax) were noted to potentially increase cost of living, so trade-offs should be considered and mitigations (e.g., channel tax revenue back to citizens) suggested.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public willingness to adopt behavioural changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Measures of what behavioural changes members of the public are willing to make (e.g., reduce single-use plastics, increase recycling, shift to active/public transport, pay more for low-carbon goods/electricity).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: More than 80% willing to reduce single-use plastics, increase recycling, and increase walking/cycling/use of public transport; fewer than 50% willing to pay more for low-carbon electricity, goods that emit more greenhouse gases, or reduce air travel. Use these willingness indicators to design policies and incentives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public understanding and support for specific decarbonisation measures
rubrics_metrics.description: Degree to which respondents understand each measure and support its adoption (e.g., solar deployment, minimum energy performance standards, industry energy efficiency).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For each measure >75% stated they understood it; >55% supported adoption; >85% support for solar deployment, MEPS, and industry energy efficiency. Policy-makers can use these metrics to prioritise measures with high public understanding/support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency in NDCs and progress reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Transparency about how Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs) are determined and reporting interim progress.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondents suggested more transparency, including setting interim goals and regularly reporting progress of decarbonisation measures to build trust and accountability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Importance of transitioning to a low-carbon economy
rubrics_metrics.description: Public belief in the importance of Singapore transitioning to a low-carbon economy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 93% agreed it is important. Use high-level public backing to justify and communicate transition plans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employer and corporate awareness of decarbonisation impacts
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether employed respondents and their companies understand how decarbonisation affects industry competitiveness and operations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 85% of employed respondents said they understood effects on their industry; 68% said their company understood. Indicates need for corporate engagement and communication where company awareness is lower than individual awareness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Green jobs and workforce skills readiness
rubrics_metrics.description: Perception that the transition will create good jobs and whether people are aware of the skills needed for low-carbon economy jobs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 76% believed the transition will generate good jobs; 65% felt aware of required skills. Recommendations included more green skills programmes at institutes of higher learning and workforce training initiatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design, attractiveness and awareness of government incentives
rubrics_metrics.description: Attractiveness of government incentives to help companies decarbonise and public/company awareness of these incentives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 44% agreed incentives are attractive; 17% disagreed. Among those who disagreed, only 35% were aware of available incentives. Guidance: improve both design and outreach/communication of incentives to increase uptake.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of disincentives (carbon pricing and regulations)
rubrics_metrics.description: Support for policies that provide companies with stronger disincentives to emit carbon (e.g., higher carbon tax, emissions regulations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 77% agreed Singapore should put in place stronger disincentives. Of those, 64% said they'd pay more for goods/services from companies that decarbonise faster. Use combination of disincentives and consumer incentives for effectiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corporate accountability and anti-greenwashing measures
rubrics_metrics.description: Holding companies accountable to climate targets; requiring transparency for those receiving decarbonisation grants; preventing greenwashing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondents called for companies to be held accountable, for transparency of sustainability plans and grant recipients, and greater public reporting to reduce greenwashing risks. Suggest tying grants to MRV and public disclosures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of grants and support for transition planning including MRV
rubrics_metrics.description: Extent to which grants should cover areas of transition planning such as measurement, reporting and verification (MRV) of carbon emissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondents suggested extending grants to cover measurement, reporting and verification to support planning and credible decarbonisation pathways.

rubrics_metrics.name: Carbon tax design and transparency
rubrics_metrics.description: Design parameters for carbon tax: level, taxable emissions threshold, allocation of allowances, transparency of allowance allocation, revenue use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suggestions included increasing carbon tax level, lowering taxable-emissions threshold, not undermining tax impacts through allowances, transparent allocation of allowances, and channeling revenue back to citizens (particularly to support lower-income households). Also recommended implementing carbon tax alongside other measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sourcing and impacts of imported low-carbon electricity
rubrics_metrics.description: Principles for electricity import projects: consider social, economic and environmental impacts on source countries; ensure imports are from fully renewable sources; avoid over-dependence on imports due to cost/security/intermittency concerns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondents recommended careful assessment of source-country impacts and renewable-certainty for imports; balance imports against domestic deployment and energy security.

rubrics_metrics.name: Carbon capture and storage (CCS) scope and safeguards
rubrics_metrics.description: Appropriate role for CCS and conditions for its deployment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondents suggested CCS be limited to hard-to-abate sectors, coupled with measures to reduce emissions, not used to prolong fossil fuel use, avoid detriment to host storage countries, and consider direct air capture. Concerns raised about technological readiness and scalability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integrity and governance of carbon credits
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulatory safeguards to ensure carbon credits used by Singapore are of high integrity and not harmful to source countries; limits on using credits as an alternative to domestic decarbonisation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommendations: regulate credit quality, expand partner countries, require that companies using credits also present plans to reduce emissions, and prohibit credits from being a way to 'pay their way out' of decarbonisation obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maximise domestic solar deployment with lifecycle considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Policies to expand domestic solar (including subsidies for rooftop solar) while addressing materials and end-of-life disposal concerns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondents suggested maximising domestic solar deployment and subsidising rooftop installations; noted concerns about panel material sustainability and end-of-life treatment that should be addressed in policy design.

rubrics_metrics.name: Energy demand reduction and storage strategies
rubrics_metrics.description: Measures to reduce energy demand (especially cooling), incentivise lower consumption during peak, and consider long-duration energy storage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suggestions included incentives to reduce peak consumption, increasing temperatures in malls/offices/public transport, effective building design to reduce cooling demand, and exploring long-duration storage. Also consider siting of energy-intensive facilities like data centres.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diversification of power generation options
rubrics_metrics.description: Consideration of other forms of power generation such as small modular reactors (nuclear), green hydrogen, wind and hydroelectricity as part of decarbonisation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some respondents recommended exploring a wider range of generation technologies. Future consultations could explicitly cover nuclear energy and related trade-offs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transport electrification, modal shift and lifecycle impacts
rubrics_metrics.description: Policies to encourage EV uptake and active/public transport while addressing electricity demand and material sustainability for EVs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommendations: further subsidise EVs, improve EV infrastructure, regulate internal combustion engine (ICE) vehicles, reduce private vehicle numbers, and improve walking/cycling infrastructure. Concerns that EVs may increase electricity demand before grid decarbonisation and that EV production (batteries) may use unsustainable materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Waste reduction and recycling
rubrics_metrics.description: Policies to reduce waste and increase recycling rates, particularly to reduce reliance on single-use plastics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondents called for stronger waste-reduction measures and increased recycling as part of decarbonisation strategies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forestry, agriculture and food system measures
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid deforestation, explore nature-based climate solutions, promote reduced meat consumption and sustainable food production.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondents recommended nature-based solutions and demand-side changes (e.g., eating less meat), and attention to sustainable agricultural practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Climate education and behavioural change
rubrics_metrics.description: Need for public education about climate change and Singapore's decarbonisation efforts, starting young and using behavioural nudges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondents suggested increasing education in schools and public outreach to encourage behavioural change; behavioural nudges were recommended to shift consumer behaviour.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design of future public consultations
rubrics_metrics.description: Improvements to public consultation design: more consultations, more engagements, more open-ended questions, and targeted questions on areas for improvement per measure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondents hoped for more consultations and engagement, suggested use of open-ended questions and focused questions on improvement areas for each decarbonisation measure; future consultations could cover topics like nuclear energy and adaptation measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pricing and market incentives for low-carbon goods
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of pricing and incentives to make low-carbon goods more attractive and limit increases in cost of living.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suggestions included pricing low-carbon goods lower than higher-carbon alternatives, providing more incentives to companies and individuals to accelerate decarbonisation, and designing measures to avoid increasing cost of living for households.
